others.route: Permit to enter and reside (Principal Immigration Officer)

note: Kiribati: no one may enter without a permit or an exemption (Immigration Ordinance, Cap. 41, 1980 Revised Edition, s. 7); the permit to enter and reside is issued on conditions as to the profession or occupation its holder may engage in and the employer who may employ him (s. 9), and a visitor's permit covers up to four months in twelve (s. 10). The Immigration (Amendment) Acts of 1983 (removal orders) and 2002 (a residence permit for spouses of I-Kiribati, with the right to work) don't change s. 9. Reading: the Ordinance doesn't say in so many words that a visitor may not work; the route is the permit that sets the holder's occupation and employer. The employment code of 2015 has nothing on foreign workers. Read in PacLII's copies through archive.org (snapshot of 17 January 2022), since PacLII and Kiribati Immigration don't answer this client. No days are modelled.

sources.title: Immigration Ordinance (Kiribati, Cap. 41, 1980 Revised Edition), ss. 7, 9–10 (PacLII's copy, archive.org snapshot of 17 January 2022)
sources.said: No person shall enter Kiribati from any place outside Kiribati unless - (a) he is in possession of valid permit lawfully issued to him under this Ordinance ... The Principal Immigration Officer may issue a permit in the prescribed form authorising any person to enter and reside in Kiribati, upon such conditions as to the security to be furnished, the profession or occupation which such person may exercise or engage in and the employer or employers by whom he may be employed within Kiribati

sources.title: Immigration (Amendment) Act 2002 (Kiribati, No. 12 of 2002) (PacLII’s copy, archive.org snapshot of 28 August 2015)
sources.said: A residence permit entitles the holder of the permit to - (a) be in Kiribati indefinitely; (b) undertake employment in Kiribati;
